scenarios.name: Bull – AI Ethernet Champion
scenarios.notes: Ethernet becomes default AI fabric; Arista is leading AI Ethernet vendor with strong AI share, solid classic DC growth, and accelerating campus; margins stay best-in-class.

scenarios.name: Base – Strong but Shared AI Winner
scenarios.notes: AI networking is large but shared among ANET/NVDA/Cisco/ODMs; classic DC grows ~10–12%; campus grows mid-teens; margins normalize slightly below peak but remain strong.

sources: TAM $40-50B 2030 (thesis, secondary forecasts); FY2027 AI fabrics target ~$7B (Arista 2027 Outlook p15) => 8.74% CAGR to the retained $9B FY2030 value; scale-across TAM alone $15-20B by 2030 (Q2'26 call, Ullal)

revenueBuild.label: Core DC frontend + routing adjacencies
sources: FY2026 base derived: ~$13.3B fourth-raised guide (Q3'26 official captions 1090-1095) - $3.5B implied AI base - $1.25B implied campus base - $1.7634B service estimate; AI/campus bases and FY2027 targets in Arista 2027 Outlook p15

scenarios.name: Bear – Capex Hangover & Competition Bite
scenarios.notes: Hyperscaler capex slows after AI boom; NVDA/white-box/in-house designs take share; campus penetration disappoints; Arista becomes a slow-growing cyclical with some margin compression.

evidence_for: FY2026 revenue guidance raised a fourth time to ~$13.3B (+48%); initial FY2027 outlook is 38-40% growth (~$18.5B) with AI fabrics ~$7B and campus ~$2B [Q3'26 official captions 1090-1095; Arista 2027 Outlook p15].

Q3 2026 revenue $3,657.6M (+58.5% YoY, +20.5% QoQ), beating the ~$3.3B guide by 10.8%; GAAP/non-GAAP GM 63.6%/64.0%, op margin 44.9%/49.1%, diluted EPS $1.22/$1.20 [Q3'26 SEC Ex-99.1 pp1,3-4; direct-source confirm pass].

Demand visibility remains substantial: deferred revenue $6,839.5M at Q3 (+27.3% from FY2025 year-end despite -0.4% QoQ); latest RPO anchor $8.4B at 2026-06-30 with ~91% recognizable in 2 years [Q3'26 SEC Ex-99.1 p5; Q2 10-Q s_0002_c13].

Supply planning supports the raised outlook: purchase commitments $11.4B with ~80% expected for use within 12 months; management reports long-term silicon, PCB and memory agreements [Q3'26 earnings deck p7; official call captions].

AI breadth and ecosystem: EtherLink exceeded 100 cumulative customers by Q2'26; AMD, Arm, Broadcom, d-Matrix, Meta, Microsoft and Qualcomm are named partners in open rack-scale architectures [Q2'26 call; Q3'26 SEC Ex-99.1 p1].
EOS NetDL software stickiness demonstrated across top tier-1 cloud titans.
Ultra Ethernet Consortium (UEC) standardization solidifies multi-vendor Ethernet fabric traction.
evidence_against: Customer concentration ROSE: top-2 end customers 42% of FY2025 revenue (16% + 26%), up from 35% in FY2024 — management expects at least three and perhaps four 10% customers in FY2026, but this remains shipment-dependent and unconfirmed until the 10-K [10-K s_0003_c09; Q3'26 captions 1488-1509].

Nvidia Spectrum-X bundling aggressively pushes full-stack networking alongside GPUs — and Spectrum-X IS Ethernet: +2.6x YoY per NVDA Q2 FY27 call (2026-08-26), with NVIDIA networking ~$31B in FY2026 (>3x Arista's entire revenue). The 'Ethernet wins therefore Arista wins' syllogism is broken; NVLink Fusion opening to third-party XPUs (incl. AWS Trainium) undercuts the non-NVDA-accelerator optionality.

Gross margin remains below prior year despite sequential recovery: Q3'26 GAAP/non-GAAP 63.6%/64.0% vs 64.6%/65.2% a year earlier; FY2027 non-GAAP guide stays 62-64% [Q3'26 SEC Ex-99.1 p4; Arista 2027 Outlook p15].

Premium valuation limits margin of safety on capex digestion shocks; the position-size override remains a separate governance risk and must be assessed on pipeline-refreshed market data, not stale pre-print multiples.
Guidance remains supply-constrained with about two quarters of visibility; not every FY2027 order has been placed, so supply execution remains a direct revenue risk [Q3'26 official call captions].

Bullwhip exposure increased: Q3 inventory rose 26.6% QoQ to $3,209.8M and purchase commitments rose 17.5% to $11.4B, while deferred revenue slipped 0.4% to $6,839.5M [Q3'26 SEC Ex-99.1 p5; Q3'26 earnings deck pp6-7].

Anchor customers are building exit ramps: Meta extended its Broadcom custom-silicon partnership through 2029; Microsoft-authored SONiC added 800GbE; white-box market growing ~18.5% CAGR (secondary estimate).

Capital-return pause: zero buybacks in 9M 2026 versus $983.0M in the prior-year period; diluted-share assumptions should remain flat rather than assume 1-2% annual shrinkage [Q3'26 SEC Ex-99.1 pp3,6].
open_questions: What does the Q3 10-Q show for gross deferred-revenue churn, RPO, inventory composition, purchase-commitment maturities and strategic-investment gains?
What is the pace of optical migration from 800G DSP to 1.6T LPO/CPO?
Will enterprise/campus segment revenue diversify total revenue beyond 40% non-cloud?
What do third-party share data (Dell'Oro/Crehan/IDC) show for Spectrum-X vs EtherLink ports in 2026 AI back-end builds?
Does the FY2026 10-K disclose a third >=10% customer (prediction anet-third-10pct-customer-fy26)?

predictions.claim: Arista reports AI-related revenue >= $1.5B in FY2025/2026 filings
predictions.notes: Resolved FALSE on review 2026-10-23: the FY2025 10-K and FY2026 10-Qs contain no AI-revenue line item (verified via filings adapter) — Arista discloses AI goals only in earnings calls/IR. The prediction was mis-specified (it bet on disclosure behavior, not operations). Superseded by anet-ai-fabrics-fy26, which resolves against the earnings-call goal.

predictions.claim: Combined revenue share of top 2 customers drops below 38% in FY2025 10-K
predictions.notes: Resolved FALSE 2026-10-23: FY2025 10-K (filed 2026-02-17) shows the two >10% end customers at 16% and 26% = 42% combined (10-K s_0003_c09, confirm pass 80%). Concentration rose from 35% (FY2024), not fell.

predictions.claim: Arista reports FY2026 AI fabrics revenue >= $3.5B (the implied FY2026 base in the Q3 2026 outlook materials)
predictions.notes: Falsification driver for the ai-backend leg. The FY2027 target is ~$7B / ~100% growth from the implied $3.5B FY2026 base (Arista 2027 Outlook p15). Resolves on actual FY2026 reporting, not guidance.

predictions.claim: Arista reports FY2026 campus revenue >= $1.25B (the implied FY2026 base in the Q3 2026 outlook materials)
predictions.notes: Falsification driver for the campus leg. The FY2027 target is ~$2B / ~60% growth from the implied $1.25B FY2026 base (Arista 2027 Outlook p15). Resolves on actual FY2026 reporting.

predictions.claim: Arista FY2026 revenue lands >= $12.6B (the pre-Q3 full-year guide; subsequently raised to ~$13.3B)
predictions.notes: Whole-build check. Q3'26 raised the FY guide a fourth time to ~$13.3B / +48%; Q4 guide $3.9-4.0B implies $13.3023-13.4023B FY revenue when added to 9M actual. Keep open until FY2026 actual revenue reports.

predictions.claim: The FY2026 10-K (filed ~Feb 2027) discloses a third >=10% end customer beyond Microsoft and Meta
predictions.notes: Q3'26 official captions 1488-1509: management expects at least three and perhaps four 10% customers, dependent on shipping enough product through December 31. This is encouragement, not resolution; tests diversification beyond FY2025's 42% top-2.

predictions.claim: Arista reports Q3 FY2026 revenue >= $3.3B (the guidance issued with the Q2 2026 print; earnings 2026-11-03 after close)

predictions.claim: Arista FY2026 non-GAAP gross margin lands within the maintained 62-64% guidance band (i.e., no structural break below 62%)
predictions.notes: Basis clarified to non-GAAP, matching official guidance. Q3'26 non-GAAP GM 64.0% and 9M 63.4%; FY2027 guide remains 62-64%. Keep open until FY2026 actual; the driver build separately holds 39% net margin flat to 2030.

predictions.notes: Initial FY2027 outlook: 38-40% growth / ~$18.5B [Arista 2027 Outlook p15]. Falsifies the revised whole-company driver trajectory if actual revenue materially undershoots.

predictions.notes: FY2027 target ~$7B / ~100% growth [Arista 2027 Outlook p15]. Tests the new near-term base for the AI driver; scale-up is not expected to be material until 2028.

decision_journal.situation: Driver-model pilot (WO-4c): base scenario now carries a sourced four-driver revenue build (AI fabrics 45x0.2=9.0B + classic DC 6.2x1.11^4=9.4B + campus 1.25x1.15^4=2.2B + service 1.43x1.15^5=2.9B = $23.5B FY2030, 39% net margin, 1,276M shares -> derived EPS $7.18, ~21% CAGR from FY2025 EPS $2.74 — a cross-check ABOVE the scenario's 0.18, so the scenario params stay conservative and unchanged). Anchors verified this session: FY2025 revenue $9,005.7M (+28.6%), GM 64.1% [10-K, confirm 80%]; Q2'26 $3,035.7M (+37.7%), FY2026 guide raised 3x to $12.6B with AI fabrics >=$3.5B and campus >=$1.25B goals [Q2'26 call]. Two stale predictions resolved FALSE: anet-top2-cust-conc-fy25 (42% actual, concentration ROSE) and anet-ai-rev-fy25 (mis-specified — Arista never discloses AI revenue in SEC filings; superseded by anet-ai-fabrics-fy26 which resolves against the earnings-call goal).
alternatives_rejected: Raise base epsCagr from 0.18 toward the driver-implied ~0.21 (rejected: the driver build is one day old and its inputs rest on guidance-era anchors; let it survive one quarterly reconciliation before promoting it into scenario parameters).

Keep anet-ai-rev-fy25 open until its 2026-11-15 target date (rejected: the evidence is already dispositive — no AI-revenue line exists in either filing; leaving it open just defers a known-false resolution).
Add drivers to bull/bear scenarios too (rejected: pilot scope is ANET base only until it survives one reconciliation cycle, per WO-4c guardrail).

decision_journal.situation: Deep-research synthesis (docs/research/tickers/anet-deep-research-2026-10.md; confirm pass 12/12 verified). Operations confirmed strong: Q2'26 $3,035.7M +37.7%, RPO $8.4B at 2026-06-30 (belief_state corrected from stale $6.1B FY25 figure), Q3 guide ~$3.3B for the 2026-11-03 print. Structural evidence turned bear-ward: NVIDIA Spectrum-X is Ethernet and grew 2.6x YoY (NVDA Q2 FY27 call), breaking the 'Ethernet wins therefore Arista wins' bull syllogism; GAAP GM fell to 62.9% from 65.2%; zero buybacks in H1'26; top-2 concentration at 42% with both anchors building exit ramps (Meta-Broadcom custom silicon through 2029, Microsoft SONiC 800GbE). Scenario weights re-weighted bull 0.40->0.35, bear 0.10->0.15 (base 0.50 unchanged); epsCagr/exitPe unchanged pending the driver build's first reconciliation. Derived block recomputed with the lab.js engine (trailing EPS $3.17, price $177.24, horizon 5): expectedMultiple 1.469 (was stale at 28.85, an old weighted-exit-PE snapshot), expectedCagr 8.0% (was 7.28% stale; note the old weights on refreshed market data would have read 9.29%), probability-weighted exit P/E 30.3x. POSITION SIZING OVERRIDE ACKNOWLEDGED: ~26% of portfolio vs ~3% scaled Kelly and $100-130 fair value vs $181 price — a deliberate discretionary override, not model-supported; the October drawdown (~-18% from the 2026-10-09 high) is the market testing exactly that gap.
alternatives_rejected: Trim toward the model-justified ~3% scaled Kelly (rejected for now: demand evidence is verified strong and the Q3 print in 6 days is the designed reconciliation point; the override is documented here with explicit kill conditions instead of an immediate mechanical trim into a sentiment-driven drawdown).

Raise bear to 0.20+ (rejected: every bear leg is live but none is confirmed — GM is declining within guide, Spectrum-X growth has not shown up as Arista share loss, and the credit-financing crack is macro sentiment, not an observed order change).

Leave bear at 0.10 until the Q3 print (rejected: two resolved predictions already went bear-direction and the 0.10 weight contradicted the thesis's own evidence_against list; evidence-weighted honesty argues for moving now, modestly).

decision_journal.situation: Q3 FY2026 deep-research and thesis reconciliation (docs/research/tickers/anet-q3-2026-deep-research.md; fresh-context confirm pass verified 10/10 factual and arithmetic claim groups). Revenue $3,657.6M (+58.5% YoY) beat the ~$3.3B guide by 10.8%, resolving anet-q3-fy26-print TRUE; GAAP/non-GAAP GM 63.6%/64.0%, op margin 44.9%/49.1%. FY2026 guide raised a fourth time to ~$13.3B / +48%; initial FY2027 outlook ~$18.5B with AI fabrics ~$7B and campus ~$2B. Base drivers rebased from $23.5B / $7.18 EPS to $24.5849B / $7.49 EPS, with service and core residuals explicitly marked as estimates. Scenario probabilities and epsCagr/exitPe remain unchanged: the driver build's FY2025-FY2030 CAGR is a cross-check, not the engine's rolling-five-year assumption, and independent AI share evidence is still absent. Bear watch increased rather than disappeared: inventory +26.6% QoQ, purchase commitments +17.5% to $11.4B, deferred revenue -0.4% to $6,839.5M, zero 9M buybacks. The discretionary position-size override remains subject to pipeline-refreshed market data and derived Kelly, not pre-print valuation fields.
alternatives_rejected: Raise bull probability or base epsCagr after one exceptional print (rejected: FY2027 figures are guidance, customer concentration and independent share remain unresolved, and the driver CAGR uses a different time base from the engine).

Lower bear probability because the near-term miss branch failed (rejected: inventory and binding supply commitments rose while deferred revenue stalled; Q3 10-Q churn and inventory detail are still pending).

Change position size from stale pre-print expected-return fields (rejected: the scoped sync still carried pre-Q3 EPS $3.17 and the pre-release close, producing expectedCagr 8.91%; wait for the pipeline to ingest Q3 actuals and a post-print price before reassessing the documented override).
